title: First damage: temporary loss of prior favor-degree—hatred while the fall lasts, election unrevoked
source_text: XLVII. Primum malum sive damnum est exclusio peccantis ab eo gradu favoris divini quo prius a Deo diligebatur. Quamvis enim, quum renatus & electus in grave quoddam peccatum labitur, & aliquandiu in eo perseverat, Deus non propterea re-vocet aeternum propositum eum salvandi & glorificandi, juxta quod futurum est, ut Deus det ipsi gratiam a lapsu illo resurgendi, & sic ad destinatum finem perveniendi; tamen pro tempore illo quo peccato isto involutus manet, non amplius placet Deo, sicut antea placebat, sed incurrit in Dei odium atque displicentiam, secundum generalia Scripturae pronunciata, quibus declarat Deum odisse omnes qui iniquitatem operantur, & eum non delectari in iis qui se subducunt.
pass_a_gloss: The first evil or damage is the exclusion of the sinner from that degree of divine favor by which he was formerly loved by God. For although, when a regenerate and elect person falls into some grave sin and perseveres in it for some time, God does not on that account revoke the eternal purpose of saving and glorifying him, according to which it will come to pass that God give him grace to rise from that fall and so arrive at the destined end; yet for that time in which he remains involved in that sin he no longer pleases God as he formerly pleased, but incurs God’s hatred and displeasure, according to the general pronouncements of Scripture by which it declares that God hates all who work iniquity, and that he is not delighted in those who withdraw themselves.
pass_b_english: First loss: while a grave fall lasts, the regenerate loses the prior degree of divine favor and incurs hatred.
Election’s saving purpose stands; present pleasing does not.
